findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage and snapshots are written in cleartext with no KMS protection.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database to untrusted networks and credential brute-forcing. The db_endpoint output further advertises the address.

The master username is the predictable default 'admin' and the password is supplied via a plain Terraform variable rather than a managed secret (Secrets Manager / manage_master_user_password), so it lands in state and plan output in cleartext.
IAM database authentication and CloudWatch log exports are not enabled, leaving only static password authentication with no auditable access record for a publicly reachable database.

The EC2 user_data script interpolates var.password and the DB username into a PHP config file; user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service (IMDSv1 is not disabled) and stored unencrypted in the instance configuration, leaking database credentials.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled; combined with a web-facing PHP application this permits SSRF-based theft of the instance profile credentials and the secrets embedded in user data.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance volume — which stores the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file — may be unencrypted at rest.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the EC2 instance profile. Any compromise of the internet-facing web server yields account-wide control of storage, compute and databases, including privilege escalation via ec2:RunInstances with existing roles.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and C2 path with no network boundary.
The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1 (nor is an equivalent enforced elsewhere), so unencrypted client connections to the publicly accessible database are permitted.
